title: chart — a plot on the plane

scenes.title: chart — a plot on the plane
scenes.description: Three charts, one element each: sampled draws with a live ±1 s.d. band, a static series, and a slider-driven curve on a fixed domain.
scenes.markdown:
# `chart`

Each plot below is **one element**. The series are real lines in the viewport — crisp at any angle — and the paper (axes, ticks, titles, grid) is drawn on the plane the way a `tensor` draws its labels, so it tilts with the plot and never piles up with screen labels. Use the **Iso** view to see that.

**Top left — `yExpr`, live.** 64 dot products of random unit-variance vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$, from the transformer domain: `tfDotSample(i, n)`. Two `hlines` at $\pm 1$ s.d. of a 4,000-draw run. Drag **n** and the band widens like $\sqrt{n}$ while the domain re-fits.

**Top right — the same draws, $\div\sqrt{n}$.** Same series divided by `sqrt(n)`; the band refuses to grow. This pair is the variance argument for the $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ scaling, and it replaces twelve hand-placed elements in the transformer lesson.

**Bottom left — `y`, static.** Literal values, built once, zero per-frame cost, drawn as points.

**Bottom right — a fixed domain.** `sin(k x)` with `xExpr` and a fixed `yDomain`, so the slider is seen to move the curve rather than the axis.

sliders.label: n — dimension of the generic vectors

add.label: q·k, i.i.d. draws
add.prompt: 64 sampled dot products of random vectors with independent zero-mean unit-variance components, from the transformer domain library. The two lines and the band are plus and minus one standard deviation of a 4,000-draw run. Drag n: the spread grows like sqrt(n), and the y domain re-fits so the axis end labels tell you the scale.

add.label: same draws, ÷√n
add.prompt: The same 64 draws divided by sqrt(n). The y domain is FIXED at -4..4 on purpose: with an auto domain the band would look the same at every n, which is true but invisible. Here the band holds its width while n climbs to 64.

add.label: static points
add.prompt: Eight literal values drawn as points. No expression, so no per-frame work: this chart costs nothing after it is built.

add.label: sin(kx)
add.prompt: A curve on a fixed domain: xExpr spaces 120 samples over one turn and yExpr is sin(k x). Both domains are fixed so dragging k visibly changes the curve, not the axes.
